match.reason: No bank point teaches entrepreneurs responding to changing conditions with new ideas and technology; the closest, bus-entrepreneurship-innovation, covers entrepreneurs and innovation in general, from a Year 11 Business Studies course, without the change-driven focus of this brief.

draft.title: Entrepreneurs and change
card: An entrepreneur is a person who spots an opportunity and takes a risk to start or grow a business. They may lose money if the idea fails.
Conditions change over time. Examples are new technology, shifts in what people want, and concern about the environment. Each change can create a need that no business yet meets.
Entrepreneurs respond with new ideas and technology. Some turn waste into products, such as making building bricks from recycled plastic.
Others sell clean energy, such as solar panels, as more households want lower power bills and less pollution. Success is not guaranteed, but a good response can create jobs and new goods.
draft.remember: Entrepreneurs turn changing conditions into business opportunities, by using new ideas and technology.

a.q: Which is the best example of an entrepreneur responding to change?
opts: Ava starts a firm that turns old tyres into playground mats
Ben keeps running his shop exactly as it was ten years ago
Chloe takes a wage from a firm that has set hours and tasks
Dan waits for the government to fix a problem in his town
a.why: Ava sees waste as an opportunity and uses a new idea to make a product, taking a risk to do so. Ben also owns a business, but he is not responding to any change.
a.clue: Look for a new idea that answers a changing need.

b.q: Solar panels become cheaper and more households in Perth want lower power bills. Tom sets up a firm selling and installing panels. Why is Tom an entrepreneur?
opts: He acts on a changing condition and risks his own money
He works for a large energy firm and is paid a regular wage
He is sure to make a profit because demand for panels rises
He copies a business that already exists in the same suburb
b.why: Tom spots an opportunity created by changing conditions and takes a risk to act on it. Rising demand does not guarantee a profit, because the business could still fail.
b.clue: Think about risk and responding to a change.

a.best: Ava starts a firm that turns old tyres into playground mats

b.best: He acts on a changing condition and risks his own money
